answer: An anti-Sybil design is a reputation graph with costly, verifiable endorsements. Each identity is a vertex whose standing grows only through useful work attested by independent peers, like a trellis that supports growth gradually rather than instantly. Newcomers start in a harbor with limited privileges and must earn trust over time, so creating thousands of fake identities buys no immediate influence. An attacker must pay real time, computation, or collateral for every vertex, while honest peers can revoke endorsements when abuse appears, making mass forgery expensive and slow to scale.
